newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran jails bank official for embezzling $3.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Iran jails bank official for embezzling $3.7 mln.

text.p: An Iranian court sentenced a state bank director to 10 years in jail for embezzling $3.7 million, a Tehran newspaper said on Thursday.

The evening daily Kayhan said the court also ordered the unnamed director of the central branch of the state-run Bank Melli Iran in the southwestern city of Abadan to pay fines amounting to twice the misappropriated sum of 11 billion rials ($3.7 million).
The case follows a series of trials for embezzlement and fraud at state agencies and banks which have featured prominently in the press and sparked a wide public outcry.
Iran's Islamic leaders have reacted to reports of corruption by demanding tougher action by courts and watchdog bodies.
In the biggest fraud case in Iran's history, an Iranian businessman was executed last year after a court found him guilty of defrauding Bank Saderat of $21.7 million. ($1 =
3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
